title: Map Sum Pairs
description: Brute force to optimized: a hash map scanned for every sum() call versus a trie caching running sums at each node.

blocks.text: 1. Problem Statement
Problem Summary: Design a MapSum with insert(key, val) (insert or update a key-value pair) and sum(prefix) (return the sum of values for all keys starting with the given prefix).

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","A sequence of insert(key,val) and sum(prefix) calls"],["Output","sum returns the total value of all keys with that prefix"],["Goal","Cache a running sum at every trie node to answer sum() in O(prefix length)"],["Constraints","Up to 50 calls, keys/prefixes up to 50 characters"]]}

blocks.text: 2. Pattern Detection

blocks.content: {"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["\"Sum of values for all keys with a given prefix\"","A trie where each node caches the running sum of all keys passing through it"],["Keys can be UPDATED (re-inserted with a new value)","Track the delta (change) in value and propagate it along the key's path when updating"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Understand the Problem

Since sum(prefix) is asked repeatedly, caching the sum of values for every key passing through each trie node (updated incrementally on each insert) lets sum(prefix) be answered directly by walking to that prefix's node and reading its cached sum, in O(prefix length).

blocks.title: Analogy: A Filing System Where Each Folder Displays the Total Value of Everything Inside It
blocks.text: Picture a nested folder system where each folder shows a running total of the value of every file inside it (including subfolders). Looking up the total for any folder is instant, just open it and read the displayed total, rather than manually adding up every file inside every time.

blocks.caption: Each trie node caches the running sum of all keys passing through it, making sum(prefix) an O(prefix length) lookup

blocks.text: 4. Understand with Examples
Example: insert("apple",3), sum("ap"), insert("app",2), sum("ap")
Results: null, 3, null, 5. After inserting "app" with value 2, sum("ap") becomes 3+2=5.
5. How Should We Think?

Before scanning all keys for every sum(prefix) call, notice that if each trie node caches the running sum of all keys passing through it, sum(prefix) becomes a direct O(prefix length) walk-and-read, and insert() just needs to add the VALUE CHANGE (delta, accounting for possible updates to an existing key) along the key's path.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: If a key is inserted for the first time, its full value should be added to every node along its path.

Observation 2: If a key is RE-inserted with a new value (updating it), only the DIFFERENCE (delta) between the new and old value should be added along its path, not the full new value (which would double-count the original contribution).

Observation 3: Tracking each key's current value in a separate hash map lets this delta be computed directly: delta = new_value - old_value (0 if the key is new).

Observation 4: sum(prefix) then simply walks to that prefix's node (if it exists) and returns its cached running sum, or 0 if the prefix path does not exist.

This leads to maintaining a trie with cached sums per node, plus a separate hash map tracking each key's current value; insert() computes and propagates the delta, sum() reads the cached value directly.
6. Brute Force Solution
Store all key-value pairs in a hash map. For sum(prefix), scan every key, summing the values of those starting with the prefix.
Why the code is written this way

items: A hash map directly supports insert() in O(1) and correctly computes sum() by scanning.
Scanning every key for every sum() call costs O(total keys times key length), unnecessary once a trie caches running sums.

blocks.text: 7. Analyze the Brute Force

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(1) for insert, O(total keys times key length) for sum.
Space: O(total key characters).
Limitation: caching a running sum at each trie node lets sum() be answered in O(prefix length), independent of the number of keys.
8. Optimize the Solution

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: Maintain a trie where each node caches the sum of values for every key passing through it. Also maintain a hash map of each key's current value, so re-inserting an existing key can compute the correct DELTA (new value minus old value) to propagate, rather than the full new value (which would double-count). insert() walks the key's path, adding the delta to every node along the way (creating nodes as needed); sum() walks to the prefix's node and returns its cached sum directly.
Maintain a trie with per-node cached sums, plus a hash map of current key values. insert() computes the delta and adds it along the path; sum() reads the cached value at the prefix's node.
9. Optimized Solution
Dry run for insert("apple",3), sum("ap"), insert("app",2), sum("ap")

blocks.content: {"headers":["Call","Delta","Effect"],"rows":[["insert(\"apple\",3)","+3","nodes a,ap,app,appl,apple each get +3"],["sum(\"ap\")","-","reads cached sum at node \"ap\" = 3"],["insert(\"app\",2)","+2 (new key)","nodes a,ap,app each get +2 more"],["sum(\"ap\")","-","reads cached sum at node \"ap\" = 5"]]}

blocks.text: Why This Works

Since every node along a key's path represents a prefix of that key, adding the key's value (or, on update, the DELTA from its previous value) to every node along the path correctly maintains each node's cached sum as "total value of all keys passing through here." sum(prefix) then directly reads this cached value at the prefix's node, in O(prefix length), correctly reflecting the sum of all matching keys' current values.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(key length) for insert, O(prefix length) for sum.
Space: O(total key characters).
10. Complexity Comparison

blocks.content: {"headers":["Solution","Time","Space","Interview Recommendation"],"rows":[["Hash map, scan for sum()","O(1) insert, O(total keys times length) sum","O(total key characters)","Correct, but slow sum() queries."],["Trie with cached sums","O(length) for both","O(total key characters)","The expected, efficient solution."]]}

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways
Map Sum Pairs demonstrates caching an aggregate (sum) directly at each trie node, turning a potentially expensive prefix query into an O(prefix length) direct lookup.
Common Mistakes

items: Adding the FULL new value instead of the DELTA when updating an existing key, causing double-counting.
Forgetting to track each key's current value separately, making delta computation impossible on updates.

blocks.text: Edge Cases

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","Expected Behavior"],"rows":[["sum(prefix) for a prefix never inserted","Returns 0."],["Re-inserting the same key with a different value","The old value's contribution is correctly replaced, not added on top."]]}

blocks.text: Interview Tips
Explicitly explaining the delta-tracking mechanism for handling key updates correctly is the key subtlety to address clearly.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "aggregate query (sum/count) over all keys with a given prefix", think: cache the aggregate directly at each trie node.
Interview Follow-up Questions

items: How would you support deleting a key entirely?

blocks.text: Pattern Connections

items: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree), the foundational structure this problem extends with cached aggregates.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The hash map approach costs O(total keys times length) per sum() call; the trie with cached sums costs O(length) for both operations, the standard efficient solution.
12. Final Summary

items: Pattern: cache an aggregate (sum) directly at each trie node, updated incrementally via delta tracking.
Core Idea: insert propagates the value delta (accounting for updates) along the key's path; sum reads the cached value at the prefix's node directly.
Time: O(total keys times length) per sum() for the hash map approach, O(length) for both operations in the trie approach.
Most Important Observation: tracking each key's current value separately allows correct delta computation on updates, avoiding double-counting.
Interview Difficulty: a practical trie extension problem, testing careful handling of updates.
One line memory trick: cache running sums per trie node; propagate the value delta on insert/update.
